annotation.title_clean: The impact of different ethical frameworks underlying a robot's advice on charitable donations
annotation.title_en: The impact of different ethical frameworks underlying a robot's advice on charitable donations
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kim, B.; Wen, R.; Zhu, Q.; Williams, T.; Phillips, E.
annotation.venue: Conference paper (HRI/RO-MAN-type conference), via ResearchGate/UMBC ScholarWorks
annotation.summary_en: Laboratory HRI experiment in which a Pepper robot gave moral advice on donating lottery tickets to charity, grounded in either deontological or Confucian role ethics. Confucian role-based advice produced more donations. It is a behavioral study of robot persuasion, not a governance document.
key_provisions_or_claims: Confucian role ethics advice from a robot induced more donations than deontological advice.
Participants who felt closer to other students donated less after deontological advice.
Framing a robot's moral messages with Confucian role ethics may promote prosocial behavior.
Study used a physically co-located Pepper robot in a lab with university students.
